newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn raps German NATO general for Bosnia remarks.
newsitem.headline: Bonn raps German NATO general for Bosnia remarks.

text.p: Germany rapped one of its generals over the knuckles on Saturday for saying peacekeepers should stay on in Bosnia for another two or three years.
The defence ninistry said remarks by General Dieter Stoeckmann, chief of staff of NATO's Central European Allied Land Forces, were "unauthorised and incorrect".
A spokesman said Stoeckman had no right to say how long troops should stay after the one-year peacekeeping force (IFOR) mandate runs out in December.

Stoeckmann told journalists on Friday after NATO exercises in Munster, northern Germany, peacekeeping troops were needed in Bosnia for up to three more years because the situation would continue to be unstable.

A post-IFOR force should include German troops, Stoeckmann said. German politicians have recently advocated extending a military presence for an extra year while NATO partners have tended to keep silent on the issue.

"The remarks by General Stoeckmann, that the presence of international peacekeeping troops in Bosnia -- including German army troops -- is necessary for two to three more years, are unauthorised and incorrect," the spokesman said in a statement.
"The general has no right to determine the length of time a "post-IFOR" force -- which has not even been decided yet -- should stay," he said.

"It is the responsibility of politicians and in particular the Bundestag (German lower house of parliament) to make such decisions," he added, referring to the fact that parliament must approve German military participation in peacekeeping missions.
About 50,000 troops from 34 countries are deployed in Bosnia under U.S. leadership to help implement the Dayton peace accord which ended 43 months of war last December.

NATO-led IFOR's mandate runs out in December, but plans are already underway to begin pulling out after Bosnian elections. It is still not certain whether some form of security force will remain after the official IFOR pull-out.

Germany's Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Defence Minister Volker Ruehe have both said some kind of security force was needed there until military equilibrium between the former warring parties had been established. They said that the force would probably include German troops.
